utterances.text: This "incident" took place over a number of days.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: But in connection with this incident --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At about halfway through, maybe the second day.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: 21st April that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Might have been the day, I cannot remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: You got a message -- the HVO's message to you, UNPROFOR, was, "if there are snipers attacking these 400 refugees, go find them, kill them and you have our blessing"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Did you tell the Prosecutors that in preparation for your testimony here?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: After getting that message, in fact an operation was undertaken, correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: To go find, capture or, if necessary, eliminate these snipers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: In fact some of them were captured?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Were others shot at?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Others were shot at.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Were any wounded or killed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: All that happened with the blessing of Colonel Blaskic, correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct, which was slightly odd since they were HVO soldiers, but there you go.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: That does not sound like a normal army to you, does it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: What does not sound like a normal army?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: A commander telling another force on his terrain to go kill his own men because he was unhappy with their conduct and he condoned the killing of those men. Is that something you have ever heard happen in the British army?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Soldiers in the British army would not do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: That is my point.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am clear on that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: You arrived in Bosnia on February 6th?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: And you left around May 8th?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I think it was something like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Did you have any R and R period while you were in Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: So you were there about 90 days, correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have not added them up, but 96 days, something like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Three months, 6th February, March, April, May.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: You mentioned that you learned there were three operative groups within the HVO underneath Colonel Blaskic, correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: I will just recite them as a foundation for another question, Mr. President. First operative group, Vitez/Travnik, second Kiseljak/Busovaca and third Zepce?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Correct, as I remember it.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Do you know who the commanders were within the HVO of those operative groups?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did at the time and I could find out again by reading our logs. I cannot remember them all off the top of my head four years later.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Would you like us to take a break here, or do you have a question which is going to deal with the previous question that you have just asked? As you like.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: At the court's pleasure, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: If the following question is not directly related to the operation, we could suspend now and start again at 4.10. Thank you. (3.50 pm) (A short break) (4.10 pm)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: The hearing is resumed, please have the accused brought in. (Accused brought in) Mr. Hayman.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Colonel Watters, you spoke earlier on the subject of whether Colonel Blaskic had a headquarters in Kiseljak; do you recall that subject?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: When did you first visit him in Kiseljak at a location that you believed to be his headquarters?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I said I thought he had an alternative headquarters in Kiseljak. I never visited him there.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: When is the first time one of your liaison officers first visited Colonel Blaskic in a location that was reported to you as being Colonel Blaskic's headquarters in Kiseljak?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We were told when trying to contact Colonel Blaskic in Vitez, in the Hotel Vitez, that he was in Kiseljak. That was told to us a number of times and from that we deduced that he had another headquarters in Kiseljak, because he seemed to spend a lot of time there.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Did you also learn that his parents lived outside of Kiseljak and that he would go visit them on weekends?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not know the detail, but I knew his family were from Kiseljak.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: So when you say you believed he had a headquarters in Kiseljak, you based that on the material you just stated, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: During the week -- several times when we wanted to talk with Colonel Blaskic we were told he was in Kiseljak. We assumed he had a headquarters in Kiseljak.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Did you ever hear a report that he had a headquarters staff in Kiseljak?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: You said you believed there were three levels within the HVO, or rather that the HVO could be analysed by identifying a strategic, an operational and a tactical level, do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Where does political power fit in to this hierarchy you have set forth?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At the strategic level.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: At the strategic level, do you combine at that level both political power and military command?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know the answer to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: So I take it your model does not specifically account for the exercise of political power within Central Bosnia, such as by the political -- Croat politicians?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I was talking about the structure of the military command.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: You said that you believed there was an agenda in Bosnia among Croats for a greater Croatia, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Did you ever speak to Colonel Blaskic and hear him speak about a greater Croatia?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: With the court's permission, I would like to approach and invite the witness to join me before Exhibit 29J, over which we have placed a transparency, and would like to make certain markings on it. I also invite my colleagues and Mr. Nobilo. Keeping in mind that we not obstruct the view of the court, you have stated that historically, conflicts in Central Bosnia have centred largely on control of the major roads --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Hayman, could you speak into the microphone, please? Everyone must have a microphone, everybody must be able to speak and hear and see. Fine, go ahead, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: You have said that in your view military conflicts in Central Bosnia have centred largely, at least in modern times, on struggles for control of the major roads and access roads, routes, correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: You need to speak into one of several microphones?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I said that, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: You know that to be true during the World War II time period, for example?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not pretend to be an expert on it, but it was certainly one of the things that we discussed and read about, the problems that the German army had subduing the Balkans during World War II.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: In part, this reality is due to the fact that Central Bosnia is an area of very high and highly defined mountains, correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Most of those mountains, you cannot go over the mountain, you must find a road or a path, for example, through a mountain pass in order to enter another part of Central Bosnia, correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: And also the winters are quite severe, with snow and ice and so forth, further hindering transportation, correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Extremely severe.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: You have been so kind as to set forth at least some of the major roads or potential access routes into Central Bosnia from the south. I would like to ask you a few questions to round out that picture. First of all, you have noted in green that the stretch of road from Kacuni to Bilalovac was taken control of by the BiH Army, correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As far as we know, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Was that in roughly the second half of January 1993, to your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was not there, but I think that is about right. It certainly was my experience when travelling that route that you went through BiH checkpoints in roughly those areas.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: By the time you arrived on February 6th that was the case?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As far as I remember, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Unless you disagree, I am going to put --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Excuse me. Your Honour, if there is going to be drawing, I would ask that the witness do the drawing and not Mr. Hayman.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: That is fine, your Honour. I would ask you to indicate again just the area of BiH control over this road, perhaps by tracing the road but also putting a right-angled line at either end so we have a record of that on the transparency.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I will, but it is four years after the event and my detail is not --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Yes, I see.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: If you would also trace --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Would you please explain? The Tribunal cannot see anything. What colour is he using to make his markings on the transparency? If you could please reindicate what we are going to see, because we have not seen anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: With the court's permission I will mark over the witness markings, indicating a right angle cutting the road from Kacuni to Bilalovac in green, first at the Kacuni point and then at the Bilalovac point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Very well, Mr. Hayman. Now we can see. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Let me direct your attention, can you find a road on this map from roughly the Kacuni area to Fojnica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I can. It is marked in yellow. There is one just there.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: In your experience, was that road held by the BiH Army throughout your tour in Central Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: The road from Kacuni to Zenica, do you see that road?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Could you please indicate to the Trial Chamber what it is, because we cannot see anything yet, the road from Kacuni to Zenica, please, as indicated by the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: I am withdrawing that question for the moment, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Very well. But we have not seen anything for the moment, so next question, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Can we find a road, Colonel, from Fojnica to Sarajevo through Tarcin?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am not familiar with it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Hayman, could you tell us where you are heading? It would be simpler. Where do you want to get to, because we are now drawing routes on a map like a travel agency, so would you please -- I know that he is not listening. Mr. Hayman, what is the goal of these various questions that you are asking? Could you tell us that? You are dealing with judges. Because for the moment we are just drawing routes. What is the objective of your question, so that we can focus things a little bit, instead of just asking the Colonel to draw routes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Of course, your Honour. The witness drew one section of road on the map that is Exhibit 29J proper as being controlled by the BiH Army, but only one section. In reality, it is at least the Defence's position that the vast majority of these roads came to be controlled by the BiH Army and in fact the witness has described a military action in April, I believe April 21st, 22nd 1993, which led to a cutting of the road from Vitez to Busovaca by the BiH Army. We wish to show the court that picture. If this was a struggle for roads, was it important only for the HVO or was this also a critical military issue for the BiH Army and if so, in what ways.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: You see, it is much simpler to explain and then to ask the witness to make the plan in accordance with your thesis. Very well then, let us hear the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: I will ask the questions from there and ask my colleague Mr. Nobilo to assist the witness and perhaps we can proceed more quickly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: I think that would indeed be simpler.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Colonel, would you agree that the mountain road from Zenica to Travnik -- do you know that road, not to Vitez but to Travnik?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I do not.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Perhaps Mr. Nobilo, can you point out the road for the witness from Zenica to Travnik. Did you become aware, Colonel, during your tour in Bosnia, that that road came to be under the control of the BiH during the period of April and May 1993?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I travelled that road during that period and it seemed to be rather muddled. There were Croat villages and BiH villages so there was not a clear route through it for either force.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Were you in the theatre when Guca Gora was overrun by the BiH army?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I was not.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Guca Gora is up in that area, correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: You are unable to tell us anything about who controlled that road?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As I said, I travelled it during the period April/May and I do not think anyone actually controlled it. Various areas of the route were controlled depending on the ethnic majority of each village on the route. I remember going through a variety of different checkpoints and on several occasions being refused access by both BiH and HVO.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: So you recall it as being contested, or having multiple checkpoints on it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I do, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: When you arrived in the theatre, were you briefed on the fighting in Gornji Vakuf that had already occurred?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, and I visited Gornji Vakuf on three or four occasions.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: In the course of the briefings you received, did you learn that the fighting in Gornji Vakuf began as early as June 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot recollect the exact dates, but I know it predated our arrival there as BritBat.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: At the time you arrived, what were you told, in terms of your briefings, in terms of who controlled Gornji Vakuf?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The battle ebbed and flowed and we were not sure actually who controlled it for the whole period. I would not be qualified to comment, as it was specifically looked after by one of our company commanders.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Did you learn in the course of your tour who controlled Konjic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Where is Konjic?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: I would ask Mr. Nobilo to assist and point out the city of Konjic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not have a recollection, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Very well. How about the city of Bugojno?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I remember we had a liaison officer responsible for Bugojno. It was not a particular area I had studied.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: During your tour, do you know whether the BiH was able to travel from Zenica to Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I suspect they could.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Do you know what route was possible for them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I do not.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Would you agree that being able to make that trip and have that access was of critical strategic importance to the BiH Army?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I would.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: In addition to having as much access to the roads that you have outlined on this exhibit as possible, correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know how they did it and I have to confess, given the state of the conflict in Sarajevo, it was always a bit of a mystery, but certainly they did appear to come in and out of Sarajevo from Zenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: In addition to having that access, would you agree that it was of critical strategic importance to the BiH Army to be able to link up the different Corps, corpuses, that they had in the theatre, correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It certainly would be a strategic aim to do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: You knew, in the course of your tour, that the BiH first corpus was in the Sarajevo and Visoko area, correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: And the second corpus was in the Tuzla, Usera and Zepce area, correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: The third corpus was in Zenica, correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: And the fourth corpus was in the Mostar, Jablanica and Konjic area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I knew in theory, I had never been there.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: And the sixth corpus was based in the city of Konjic, were you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was not, actually.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: And the seventh corpus was located in Travnik, you were aware that they were headquartered in that city?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I was. I was not actually sure they were a Corps, I thought Travnik was subordinate to Zenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: You thought they were part of the 3rd Corps?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: In any event it would have very important --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Slowly, Mr. Hayman, please. Do not forget the interpreters.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: My apologies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: And of course us. Think of us too. Continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: We are always thinking of you, Mr. President and your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: With respect to the third corpus and the BiH forces in Travnik, similarly road access between those two units would be of critical military significance to the BiH Army?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Would you agree in principle that control of these roads was of critical military significance to both the HVO and the BiH Army?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I would.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Would you agree that in January 1993, or at least prior to your arrival, the BiH Army took steps to attain control over a portion of these roads, specifically the stretch between Kacuni and Bilalovac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot remember what went on before we arrived. Certainly during our tour, that stretch of road was contested by the HVO and BiH and to my memory was largely controlled by the BiH.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: You have described on 21st April 1993 how the junction at Kaonik had been overrun and taken control of by the BiH Army, correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Perhaps that could be indicated as well by a green cutting mark across the road in that location, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (Witness marks map).

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: The effect of that act was to sever the road link between Vitez and Busovaca, correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Would you agree that that was a further military strategic importance to the BiH Army because once the Vitez Busovaca enclave was severed, forces within the enclave could not be moved along the spinal road and massed at any one defensive point; would you agree with that, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I would.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Before we move away from this map, you have also discussed in your testimony the concept of canton 10 under the Vance-Owen Peace Plan.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: You said you believed that the conflict on 16th April and following days on the part of the HVO involved an attempt to purge canton 10 of its Muslim residents?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That was the only logic that we could think of.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Let me ask you about certain towns and villages within canton 10 and tell me whether they were attacked by the HVO on the 16th.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I will do my best.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Mr. Nobilo, if you could point out the towns as I identify them. Sivrino Selo. Do you see that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Is it necessary to show them? If I have understood you well, Mr. Hayman, that your strategy is to mention a number of villages within that canton that were not attacked, perhaps you can list them and see whether the witness can react to that. That would speed up things a little. It will not change anything in terms of the substance of your question, so please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: I will and I can, although the location of the villages is also of interest. Have you found Sivrino Selo?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is here, sir (indicates).

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Do you know, was it attacked on the 16th?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I would have to check our records. It is not a name which immediately springs to mind.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Was it attacked on 17th April, if you know, 1993?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Is Sivrino Selo on the spinal road between Vitez and Busovaca?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is a kilometre north to it.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Can you find the town or village of Krcevine? Mr. Nobilo, can you assist, please? Indicating to the north of Vitez?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Do you know, was it attacked on 16th April 1993?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Is it on the spinal road from Vitez to Busovaca?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: A kilometre north of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: The town of Poculica, do you find that on the mountain road from Vitez to Zenica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I certainly remember there was something at Poculica. It was quite heavily defended by the HVO, I remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: By the HVO or by the BiH?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I could be wrong, I thought it was a HVO town. We tried to get access to it but we could not. I have a memory of HVO, I could be wrong. There are very many towns in that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Mr. Nobilo, if you could point out for the witness the town of Tolovici, again north of Vitez. Do you recall whether it was attacked on 16th or 17th April?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I do not.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: It is not on the spinal road, is it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, it is not.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Mr. Nobilo, could you point out the town of Preocica to the witness, indicating again to the north of Vitez. This also would be in canton 10, correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I would have to overlay the boundary, but I suspect it is on the edge of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Zenica was in canton 10, was it not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot remember the exact boundary of canton 10 on this map.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Do you think the boundary fell between Vitez and Zenica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think it did.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Thank you, you may sit down. When you arrived in the theatre in February, were you briefed on what the BiH Army was doing to strengthen its position and prepare for a conflict with Croats in Central Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I was not, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Were you told that the BiH Army had undertaken a general mobilisation in the Vitez area in January 1993?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I was not. I do not quite know what a general mobilisation was. I think the whole of Central Bosnia was mobilised.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: If the usher could assist, your Honour, I have a document I would ask be placed before the witness, provided to your Honours and provided to Prosecution counsel. The first page, your Honour, is in English, the second page in BSC. We have not yet been able to have any translations undertaken, but with the court's leave we will place them on the ELMO. I can read at least the first page, perhaps Mr. Nobilo can read the second and undertake a translation for all and then I would like to ask the witness a few questions about the documents. Perhaps if you could place it on the ELMO, Colonel Watters, I can read it, you can look at it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Could we hear the number of this exhibit, please, Mr. Prosecutor? Any comments regarding this exhibit? Let us wait for the witness to identify it first.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour. At the very top of the page -- I am sorry to burden the usher again, but if we could move the document down, at the top of the page is in hand-written form "Cheshire Mil Info 080 19th January 1993"; do you see that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Do you know what "Cheshire Mil Info" would refer to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is a 1 Cheshire military information summary, probably serial number 080, dated 13th January 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: 13th or 19th?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sorry, maybe 19th. On the document it is 19th. It is difficult on the screen to say.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: If I may read it? Your Honour, parts of this document have been redacted. It was provided to us by the Prosecutor's Office and hence the first paragraph begins with 2: "2. Vitez. A local source reported that tensions in the area between Croats and Muslims were high. He stated that local Muslim civilians were being called up for duty with the local BiH forces. One particular example (call-up document attached) had never served with the BiH forces before. The document states that he was to report to the school in Preocica." Does "GR" refer to "grid reference"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: "GR 2497 on 15 January 93. The stamp on the document was that of the 325th Broska Brigade. Comment. The recruitment of civilians (i.e. people who have no involvement in the BiH/HVO forces) is a reflection of the assessed need by the BiH forces to strengthen themselves against the perceived increased threat from the HVO. A CS" -- is that a reference to "call sign"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Would that be a Warrior vehicle?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It could be a Warrior, it could be an armoured personnel carrier, it could be a Scimitar, it could be a Scorpion. It could be anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: "A CS visited the predominantly Muslim village of Preocica. It was reported then that there were well prepared defensive positions around it and that the village was of military significance in the Vitez area." Comment ends. Now the second page.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: In the heading, we find the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina, the Defence headquarters of Vitez. The heading is, "Call-up for service in the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina". In the form we first see surname, first name and father's name, but this has been redacted, crossed out. Year of birth 1967, resident of Kruscica: "Should on 15th January 1993 immediately upon receiving this call-up paper to the unit of the BH Army T-9048, the location, the school at Preocica. Take with you your personal things, warm clothing and weapons. Commander of the Defence of Vitez, signed", his signature and the stamp of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, 3rd Corps, 325th Mountain Brigade of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Do you recall, Colonel Watters, whether you were briefed when you arrived in the theatre in February on the subject of mobilisation of forces?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not specifically but generally it was believed that the entire Central Bosnia area was mobilised to form their joint union against the Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: By that, you mean that every able-bodied man had been mobilised either into the HVO or the BiH Army, correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think every able-bodied man is probably an exaggeration, but a great majority.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Do you recognise this document as being in the format of a Mil Info Summ generated by 1 Cheshire during their tour in Central Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: I offer the document, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It is going to be admitted into evidence as Defence Exhibit D59, that is the number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: We spoke a moment ago about the third corpus headquartered in Zenica. Did you receive reports in your tour that they had somewhere in the neighbourhood of 90,000 men under their command?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot remember the exact figures, but they were certainly a substantial force.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot remember.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: A substantial force. I never remember fastening on to a specific figure. I would not actually have trusted it.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Were you also told or briefed by your own personnel that the HVO within Central Bosnia had around 12,000 men at their disposal; does that sound accurate to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Again, I do not remember fastening on specific numbers. It could have been accurate, I really cannot remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Do you recall being briefed generally as to the proportion of soldiers in the HVO in Central Bosnia and soldiers in the third corpus?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, and in infantry the BiH outnumbered the HVO.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: By a large multiple?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Our assessment was by a considerable margin and the HVO outnumbered the BiH in terms of their access to direct fire tank weapons, artillery and mortars. That was our general assessment.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: When you say "direct fire tank weapons", what do you mean?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Anti-aircraft cannon mounted on the back of trucks, anti-tank weapons, tanks themselves and mortars and artillery for indirect fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Did you see the HVO in Central Bosnia in possession of any tanks?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Only in Maglaj, personally.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: What about in the Lasva Valley, did you ever see any HVO tanks?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Did you see or learn of BiH Army tanks in the Lasva Valley or Zenica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I personally saw one T-55 on the mountain road.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Let me turn your attention to the cease-fire agreement of April 18th, do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am sorry, there were so many agreements, on 16th, 17th, 18th, 19th. I cannot remember a specific one. I remember the discussions on the 16th and I remember the discussions on the 21st. I am not sure I chaired them. I think Colonel Stewart might have done.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: If I could ask for the usher's assistance, your Honour. (Pause). If a copy of this document, your Honour, could be provided to the witness as well as Prosecution counsel and each of your Honours. Again if it could be placed on the ELMO. (Handed). The first page of this document, Colonel Watters, bearing in hand-written form, "Cheshire Mil Info 170 18 April 1993." The first page reads, "Warrior CS reported a BiH CP"; would that be "checkpoint"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it would.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: "Located at grid reference 134001. The call sign reported that the soldiers were unfriendly and told the call sign to leave immediately." First let me ask, do you know how we would go about determining where this location is?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, by plotting the grid reference on the map.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Is that something we could do even on this map?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I would have to look carefully, I might be able to.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Perhaps during the evening break we could attempt that and save time. If the second page of the exhibit could be displayed, this refers to the cease-fire matter I spoke of. In the upper right-hand corner, this reads: "Annex A to Mil Info 171 18 April 1993. Copy of cease-fire agreement between HVO and BiH, distributed by" --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Is that 70 or 71? I am sorry, 170. Maybe Mr. Hayman made an error and said 171. I think it is a zero. It is not English or French, so it is 170, "Mil Info 170". Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Thank you: "Copy of cease-fire agreement between HVO and BiH, distributed by", and only the letters "HV" are visible next to the margin, but it is unclear whether something may have been cut off on the margin, "Central Bosnia. "1. The following text is taken directly from a copy of the cease-fire agreement signed by Tihomir Blaskic, commander HVO, Central Bosnia, on 18th April 1993. "'On the basis of the orders given by the HVO head of staff, HZ Herceg-Bosna office number", then a list of numbers, "dated April 18th. "A. All subordinate HVO combat units are to immediately stop all combat actions against units of the BiH. "B. Exchange the detained soldiers and civilians at once. "C. Take care of all the wounded, no matter what army they belong to. "D. Collect all information about those involved in the conflict, details on murdering of soldiers and civilians'." Colonel Watters, do you have a recollection of the process which gave rise to this apparent cease-fire agreement executed on April 18th?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I remember the cease-fire agreement, I remember it making no difference and I do not remember the -- I have no recollection of what the process was that produced it, other than the fact that it seemed to be ignored on the ground.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Would there be a record in the archives of 1 Cheshire concerning that process, assuming 1 Cheshire was involved?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: 1 Cheshire would not have been involved if it was Herceg-Bosna, the level that promulgated it. I have a recollection of this cease-fire agreement coming sort of slightly out of nowhere, and I was initially being extremely excited about it when it first arrived, thinking there had been a major break through, but as I said, it did not appear to make any difference on the ground.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: An actual cease-fire did not stick between the period of 18th April and at least 21st April?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: It did not stick, correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Is this document in the format of a 1 Cheshire Mil Info Summ and as you would expect it to be in that regard?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: I offer the document, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: We have no objection, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: What is the number then?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, this is D60.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: You spoke in your testimony of the cease-fire meeting at the ECMM house on 21st April 1993.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: You have that in mind, that meeting?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Would you agree that at the time of this meeting, the Army of BiH had either taken the Kaonik junction or was advancing on the Kaonik junction from the direction of Kuber mountain?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, sir, they had either taken it or were about to take it.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Would you agree that the army of BiH, at the time of this meeting, 21st April, was either advancing from Poculica to Preocica and Dubravica, or had already taken those positions?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Would you also agree that as at the time of this meeting, the Army of BiH was advancing towards Vitez from the direction of Krcevine to the north of Vitez, north-north-west?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was certainly advancing on Vitez from the north, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: One moment, your Honour. (Pause). To your knowledge, was the Army of BiH also advancing from Bilalovac in the direction of Kiseljak?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There was certainly fighting to the north of Kiseljak. I am not exactly sure where the forces were coming from.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Did you receive reports on 21st April 1993 concerning how many Croat villages had been lost by the HVO to the Army of BiH on that date?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I would have to go and check the records. Ground had been lost by the HVO, which would have included villages. I cannot remember the exact list.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Do you recall receiving a briefing that approximately five Croat villages had been lost or were in the process of being lost on 21st April 1993?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is quite possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: In fact, your view is, is it not, that the cease-fire agreement reached on 21st April 1993 saved the HVO from a military defeat in Central Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I would certainly say it saved them from possible defeat. I could not obviously say they would have actually been defeated. They might have held out and been reinforced from Prozor, I do not know, but they were certainly facing defeat.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: They had already lost or were about to lose the Kaonik junction; would you agree their backs were to the wall?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I would.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Now let us turn to the meeting itself. Was the subject of the meeting on the 21st in essence Petkovic's request to the BiH to stop their offensive?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You could summarise it as that, yes, but the HVO also had conditions to do with any future cease-fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: That request and the conditions and the mechanics of a cease-fire and a withdrawal, that was the subject of the meeting?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The principles were the subject of the first part of the meeting, chaired by Mr. Thebault, and the mechanics of how the two commanders would agree to separate their forces and place a cease-fire was the subject of the protracted second military planning meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: You attended both parts?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: In either part, was there any discussion of a massacre in Ahmici or any other massacre of Muslim civilians?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: No mention whatsoever in that meeting, correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have no recollection of it. I think there were a lot of accusations and counter-accusations of various things, but there were no specific accusations by the BiH of a massacre in Ahmici, I am sure of that. But there were lots of accusations and counter-accusations, and occasionally General Petkovic or General Halilovic would step in and stop the meeting descending into an argument between Mr. Merdan and Colonel Blaskic as to the prosecution of the conflict over the preceding few days. I have a clear recollection of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: In these meetings, allegations were constantly being raised and being brushed aside by the opposing party, correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Who is the opposing party?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: The enemy force. An allegation would be raised that something happened here or there, or the other side would say, "we do not know who did that", something to that effect, would try and brush it aside?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I would not describe it as "brushing aside". I would say the two strategic commanders were keen to reach a regional decision and did not want the process to get bogged down in accusations and counter-accusations which would only continue to inflame the situation, rather than bring the situation to an end. I have a clear recollection of them both being very General-like about it, rather than worrying about the tactical position on the ground vis-à-vis individual forces and villages.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: The result of this meeting was an agreement to establish a demilitarised area and in effect a withdrawal of troops, correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Would you not agree, Colonel Watters, that when the enemy is pressing in and taking territory, and that is what is being discussed, and your commander asks you if you have the situation under control, the reference to "situation" in all probability means the losses you are sustaining at that very moment with respect to the territory under your command; would you not agree with that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is an interpretation. I was not sure at the time of my own interpretation. It appeared to be quite a vitriolic exchange between the two.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: If five Croat villages were lost on 21st April 1993, can you appreciate the level of intensity of General Petkovic's feelings on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can. What I did not understand was the impact it had on the interpreter.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Would you agree that the interpretation I set forth that referenced to "control the situation" most likely refers to the losses being sustained on the ground by the HVO; would you not agree that that is a reasonable interpretation of the exchange you described as occurring on 21st April 1993?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is an interpretation, it was not altogether mine at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Do you agree it is a reasonable interpretation of the exchange that you described occurring on 21st April 1993?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is an interpretation, I am saying it was not necessarily mine at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Do you agree it is a reasonable one? If you do not --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Your Honour, please, the question was asked and I believe we are now on the third time the question was asked. The witness answered the question. Can I ask that question not be repeated because counsel is dissatisfied with the answer?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Yes, on this specific point, I have to sustain this objection. I can say to you, Mr. Hayman, with a smile on my face, that you yourself this morning objected to questions which assumed that they were going to extract from the witness a kind of interpretation that was being asked. I did not interrupt you at the present and I considered it was natural for you to try to give the invitation that you wanted, but this is three times you are asking the question and the witness has already answered, so please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: If you change your answer, let us know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Your Honour, I move to strike the comments of counsel on the record at this point and ask that the court direct counsel just to ask questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Yes, I do not like having things taken out of the transcript. We are experiencing something which is alive, that is what a trial is. Mr. Hayman made that comment, it is going to remain in the transcript then. It is not the best of his comments since the trial has begun, but it was said. All right, continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Could you understand yourself anything that was said between General Petkovic and Colonel Blaskic on 21st April 1993?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Could you see them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I could see the back of Colonel Blaskic and the face of General Petkovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: So you could not see Colonel Blaskic's facial response to this conversation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I could not.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Were you looking at them during this exchange, were you focusing on the back of Colonel Blaskic and the face of General Petkovic?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Hayman, please try to shorten what you are saying, we are not going to reconstruct a scene none of us witnessed. The witness is telling you what he saw and what he understood. Try to move to another question, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: I will move on, your Honour. I think he said what he could see, and my question is, was he looking, was he focusing on it, or is it something he could see if he looked and turned in that direction, which are two different things, and if it is too detailed I will move on, but may I just see if the witness has anything else to add?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I could see that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Colonel, yes, go ahead.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was focused on it because it was the first time I had seen a Croat military commander getting a roasting from another Croat military commander, so it was something very unusual and I focused on it.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, if we are going to 5.30 today, this might be a convenient time to go into closed session, briefly, concerning the matter that has been brought to our attention at the beginning of the day.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour, I believe we will go into that issue. I believe it is private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Yes, just no public audio.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Private session then. I would just tell the people in the visitors' gallery, this is not a closed session, they will see people here speaking, but the sound will not come through. All right, we can now pass into the private session. It will take a few moments. (In closed session)

procedural_notes.text: (Hearing adjourned until 10.00 am the following day)
